title: Close the served-but-undeclared hole in the cells namespace
action:
bee's stated law is that a verb the dispatcher serves and the registry does not declare must fail, and so must the inverse. For the cells namespace only the second half is guarded. The existing sweep `every_namespace_the_dispatcher_serves_is_declared_in_the_registry` in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests/registry_dispatch.rs scans only the devtools and herding modules — search that test for the paths it reads and you will find `verbs/cells/util.rs` is not among them. So a cells sub-verb that is served but never declared passes green today, which is exactly how this feature could ship a verb nobody can reach through the registry.

Write the missing half: a test that reads the cells dispatch table in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/cells/util.rs (the `match verb {` at util.rs:68, whose arms look like `"block" => run_block(flags, use_json, t0),` at :74) and asserts every arm it serves has a matching declaration in the registry payload.

Prove it the honest way, red first: confirm the new test FAILS when a served arm's declaration is removed, before you make it pass. A test that has never been red against the thing it guards is a test that agrees with itself.

Extend the existing sweep if that is the smaller change; write a sibling test if the existing one's shape does not take a third source. Say which you chose and why in the cap report.

truths: A cells sub-verb served by the dispatch table but absent from the registry payload fails this test by name.
The test names the offending verb, not just a count.
The test passes on the tree as it stands after sd-1.
artifacts: The served-but-undeclared assertion for the cells namespace in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests/registry_dispatch.rs
key_links: The test reads the real dispatch table in verbs/cells/util.rs, never a hand-kept list of verb names.
prohibitions: No existing assertion in registry_dispatch.rs is weakened or deleted.
No source file outside tests/ is changed by this cell.

trace.outcome: Fold the cells dispatch table into the served-but-undeclared law, proven red-first
deviations: Extended the existing sweep instead of writing a sibling law, and added one sibling BITE test — the sweep took a third source in three lines, but a green sweep cannot show it would notice a gap, so the bite belongs in its own named test — found a better route

Proved the red by removing a declaration from the test-side declared set rather than from the registry payload — packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/generated/registry_payload.json is reserved by sd-2 and live, so writing it even temporarily would have clobbered a sibling worker — hit an unforeseen obstacle
